chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from ʿAmmār ibn Marwān, from Zayd al-Shaḥḥām, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
Indeed, great reward is with great affliction, and Allah does not love a people except that He afflicts them.

key_terms.أَحَبَّ اللَّهُ: Allah loved; indicating divine favor and care
key_terms.عَظِيمَ الْأَجْرِ: great reward or immense recompense from Allah

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith explain the relationship between Allah’s love, affliction, and reward?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that greater spiritual reward accompanies greater trials. It also states that affliction can be a sign of Allah’s love for a people, indicating a divinely meaningful test rather than mere hardship.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Ammar Bin Marwan, from Zayd Al Shahham, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The great Recompense is with the great afflictions, and Allah<sup>azwj</sup> does not Love a people except that He<sup>azwj</sup> Afflicts them’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Muhammad ibn Sinan from ‘Ammar ibn Marwan from Zayd al-Shahham from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:
‘‘The greatest reward comes from greatest trials and suffering. There have never been a people whom Allah loved but were not put to trial.”
